idea-plugin.name: CodeBridge
idea-plugin.description:
Use VS Code extensions in IntelliJ-based IDEs. Browse and install them from Open VSX on a VS Code Extensions page in Settings, or install a .vsix file. Your project's .vscode folder works too: launch.json entries become run configurations, tasks.json tasks can run before them, and extensions use the settings in settings.json.

Extensions run unmodified in the real VS Code extension host, which comes with the plugin. You don't need VS Code or Node.js installed. What extensions provide shows up as ordinary IntelliJ features.

  • Extensions: search Open VSX, see details, and install, update, turn off or uninstall extensions.
  • Editing: errors and warnings, semantic colouring, syntax highlighting, hover docs, completion, signature help, inlay hints, code lenses, folding, Extend Selection and document links.
  • Navigation: Go to Declaration, Find Usages, usage highlighting, Go to Class/Symbol, the Structure view and breadcrumbs.
  • Refactoring: Rename, quick fixes and refactorings as intentions, and Reformat Code with the extension's formatter.
  • Debugging: debug with an extension's debugger in IntelliJ's debugger, using your launch.json.
  • Workspace: launch.json, tasks.json and settings.json, including multi-root .code-workspace files.
  • Extension UI: extension views as tool windows, webviews, status bar items, notifications, quick picks, progress, terminals and test runners.

Remote development (split mode) is supported: the UI stays on your machine and extensions run where the project lives.

CodeBridge is in active development. Many extensions work well, but some of what VS Code offers extensions is not available, so not every feature of an extension will work. Notebooks, source control, comments, custom editors and extensions' chat and AI features are not supported. Windows on ARM is not supported.
